name: Honey drops in eyes

lead: Honey drops in the eyes is a folk claim that diluted honey can lighten the colour of the iris. It appears in eye-colour discussions as a no-procedure route to lighter eyes and is not an established cosmetic procedure.

Proponents describe a gradual bleaching effect. General references describe eye colour as set by iris pigmentation, and no published studies tested honey for changing it. Wikipedia's honey article contains little on eye use.

paras: Folk accounts describe applying diluted honey to the eyes repeatedly over weeks or months, looking for a gradual shift in shade.
Non-sterile substances in the eye are generally associated with irritation and infection. The American Academy of Ophthalmology advised against over-the-counter lightening drops in 2024.

angle.text: A folk claim in eye-colour discussions says diluted honey applied to the eyes gradually lightens the iris. It is not an established cosmetic procedure, no studies have tested it, and ophthalmologists advise against related lightening drops.

lead: Honey drops in eyes is a folk beauty claim that putting diluted honey in the eyes will gradually lighten the color of the iris. People who try it are after lighter, more striking eyes, which many in appearance communities rank among the most noticeable facial features. [1][2]

Practitioners describe the idea as honey having a mild bleaching effect that builds up with repeated use. The American Academy of Ophthalmology describes the claim as a myth, explaining that eye color is set by the iris, so a substance on the surface cannot alter it, and warns that foreign substances can expose the eye to irritating or harmful materials. [1] Healthline's medically reviewed article says there is almost no support for the color claim, noting honey is unlikely to reach the deeper, pigmented layers. [2]
Separately, researchers have studied honey-containing preparations for eye conditions such as dry eye and corneal problems; that work concerns treatment of disease, not eye color. [2]
infobox: Described by the American Academy of Ophthalmology as a myth [1]

paras: Proponents of the folk remedy say honey mixed with water can gradually lighten eye color. [2] Instructions are not reproduced here.

Wikipedia describes eye color as depending on the amount of melanin in the iris and on how light scatters within it, with many genes involved. Color can change naturally: a 1997 study of white Americans found about 17% of children had changed eye color by adulthood, in roughly equal numbers lighter and darker. Certain glaucoma medications and trauma can increase pigmentation in one eye. [3]

The American Academy of Ophthalmology states that the iris determines eye color and advises that adding foreign substances to the eyes can expose them to irritating or harmful materials; it recommends ophthalmologist-approved colored contact lenses for anyone wanting a different look. [1] Healthline notes raw honey should never be placed directly in the eye and that homemade drops would need sterile preparation. [2]

Healthline also summarizes research on honey in medical eye preparations: a 60-person study of honey-containing artificial tears for keratoconjunctivitis, a 114-person study of honey treatments in chronic dry eye, and animal and laboratory work on antimicrobial effects. It describes these as unrelated to eye color. [2]
No studies found testing honey drops for changing eye color. Studies of honey in eye care address dry eye and infection, not pigmentation. [2]
